chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: After Moline; Stuff's Hollywood stars, Kay Francis, and the Trouville stay
summary: Autrey never saw Stuff again; he recalls Stuff introducing him to movie stars such as Kay Francis at the Trouville Club, where they stayed about a year.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Really? That was the last time you see him?
I'm trying to think now when I see --
What happened to the band? Did you go on with the band under you, or what?
Yes, we came -- we -- I came back into New York, where -- where and when? I'm trying --
That was in Moline.
Yeah, Moline, Illinois. Uh, because we had been -- I'm trying to think. How did we get to the Trouville Trouville Club?
Wasn't that before?
That's before. And it has to be, it has to have been.
You must have been coming east, then.
Yeah. Anyway, because we did all that, and man, he had a heck of a band! Oh man! I told you we had

all the -- in fact, he knew, he knew all the movie stars. He introduced me to so many people. I thought I'd met a lot of people with Pats, but naaah, he was chummy, first name, pat on the back, say well we're crazy about each other. And now I'll never forget the night, the night that he and -- uh, uh, the most beautiful woman in the world, to me, I thought, she was sitting in the audience. She'd just come back from boating. She'd been out with her boat there.
(Snap) not Tallulah. I met her two, three --
: Movie star?

Yeah, oh yeah! Quite a star. Let's see, and hey Stuffy, and he was on the bandstand, yelling to her, and she's sitting about 50 feet from the bandstand, in the back, you know. Remember that time? Says Blah, blah, blah, and I just sat there, this thing was going on, man, and she was so beautiful, so nice.
And the guy who did the Saint, part of the Saint there (snap) two brothers.
: Oh yeah, I know the two, had different names.
Yeah, and --
: Brothers, and they looked very much alike. One was -- one of them married both -- two Gabor sisters.
Right.
I know exactly who you mean. I've got the same problem you have. I can circle all the way around.

You call it -- oh, shoot, he and Stuff was having a thing, so Stuff called me over saying, you know, meet Mr. -- no, meet Mr. Autrey. Herman, this is -- hm, God doggy. That's why I hate to bring some of these subjects up here, much as I -- hmmm. Well as I know the man, and nice as he was, and he say, Mr. -- Meet Mr. Autrey. And then he called the man by his first name, and I felt like two cents. You know?
(Laughter.)
He say say something to him, let him know who you say. When are you going to play the music? I say right now! So that was my cue to get the heck away from the table. You know.
(Laughter.)
That was a good cue.
Oh yeah, you know, because I mean -- I say -- he's telling him to meet Mister Autrey, and put him down. Well, they knew each other. Kay Francis is the woman's name I'm trying to think of.
Oh, Kay Francis.
Yeah, and they were good friends, and

good pals, and they knew each other, and she loved him. They loved the band, and they had plenty going. They knew so many people that they both knew, and for so many years. I mean -- and it was -- you know -- made you feel like -- you said Wow!
How long were you out in Hollywood, this time?
With Stuff, well I had been there before, about -- almost two years.
Almost two years?
Because I left -- yeah, because well, a year or something, because we stayed there until what, January 6th we came back.
All at the Trouville? Did you play the --
Yeah. Yeah, all at the Trouville Club, yeah.
-- steady?
Yeah, until we came off. And --
